newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends steady as bulls hold their ground.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends steady as bulls hold their ground.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended firm on Wednesday after crude oil rebounded from its early losses and bullish traders said the tightness in prompt supply justified these higher prices.

Bids on NWE cargoes were heard at $230 cif and offers at $232, roughly unchanged from yesterday, sources said. Feb swaps ended up about $1 at $226.50/$227.50 a tonne and March rose 50 cents to $215.50/$216.50, they said.
Several traders were still believed to be short material for commitments to end-users this month. But one said there was a general tightness in the market.
That was after one end-user in Northwest Europe and Brazil's Petrobras each had bought 250,000 tonnes this month--unexpected purchases that dried up supplies.
And there are no unsold cargoes coming to NWE, he said.
"There are hardly any cargoes around," he said, adding that naphtha would be trading at even higher levels if crude had not tumbled so sharply this month.
Sources said a 55,000 tonne cargo was expected to load this week in Rotterdam, destination unknown.

The trader said it was originally headed for the States but it may have to stay in NWE due to a weaker U.S. market, although the large cargo may not be available immediately for NWE due to the size and nomination restrictions.

End-users, who typically want lower prices, have argued that naphtha remains overvalued relative to crude and other products. Once the prompt demand is met, prices will fall to where March swaps are trading, near $215/$216, they said.
